packages.title: ECO4 extension to 31 December 2026 QA
facts: Ofgem's ECO4 Delivery guidance was updated to reflect extension of ECO4 to 31 December 2026.
The guidance covers how suppliers meet obligations and how homes and measures qualify.
It also covers measure and project notifications, scoring, monitoring, auditing and counter-fraud processes.
Obligation compliance and measure scores are not direct greenhouse-gas measurements.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from ECO4 eligibility.

packages.title: ECO4 score monitoring versus measured emissions QA
facts: ECO4 guidance contains technical and score-monitoring requirements.
Scheme scores support administration of supplier obligations.
A scheme score is not a direct physical measurement of energy use or greenhouse-gas emissions.
Project notification status is distinct from verified delivered carbon savings.
No property emissions quantity is fabricated.

packages.title: ECO4 New Measures and Products route QA
facts: ECO4 New Measures and Products guidance covers Innovation Measure, Standard Alternative Methodology and Data Light Measure routes.
The guidance follows amendments to the ECO4 Order in 2026.
IM and DLM applications are not accepted after 31 March 2026 under the stated update.
Application eligibility is an administrative condition rather than a measured emission.
No parcel greenhouse-gas value is inferred.

packages.title: ECO4 innovation-route versus GHG QA
facts: NMAP guidance is additional to ECO4 supplier-administration and delivery guidance.
Innovation-route approval does not itself prove a realised emissions reduction.
Measure eligibility must be kept separate from measured post-installation performance.
Programme administration cannot substitute for consumption or emissions evidence.
No site emissions quantity is created.

packages.title: SECR 2026 review transparency finding QA
facts: The 2026 SECR post-implementation review examines the reporting framework introduced in 2019.
SECR replaced the previous CRC Energy Efficiency Scheme reporting framework.
The review reports improved transparency and consistency in company-level energy and carbon reporting.
It also identifies opportunities to simplify or improve the framework.
A reporting requirement is not itself a guarantee that a parcel emission has been directly measured.

packages.title: SECR reporting versus measurement QA
facts: SECR is a statutory corporate energy and carbon reporting framework.
The review considers effectiveness, proportionality and administrative burden.
Corporate disclosures depend on organisational reporting boundaries and methods.
A disclosure should not be relabelled as a site-specific measurement without supporting evidence.
No parcel emission is inferred solely from SECR applicability.

packages.title: ESOS second progress update 2026 timing QA
facts: For ESOS phase 3, the action-plan deadline was 5 December 2024.
The first annual progress update deadline was 5 December 2025.
The second annual progress update deadline is 5 December 2026.
Action-plan reporting tracks commitments and progress rather than automatically verified emissions savings.
No future December 2026 progress result is treated as observed.

packages.title: ESOS audit and action versus realised savings QA
facts: ESOS requires qualifying organisations to address energy-audit and action-plan obligations.
Action plans require board-level sign-off.
Progress updates report implementation against commitments.
An audit recommendation or commitment is not the same as a measured realised energy or carbon saving.
No parcel emission reduction is inferred without separate evidence.

packages.title: CCA target periods 7 to 9 calendar QA
facts: The 2026 CCA statutory guidance defines Target Period 7 as calendar year 2026.
Target Period 8 runs from 2027 through 2028.
Target Period 9 runs from 2029 through 2030.
The scheme administration period extends through 31 March 2033.
Target-period membership does not itself measure a facility's greenhouse-gas emissions.

packages.title: CCA 70 percent reckonable-energy eligibility QA
facts: The CCA guidance states an eligible facility test based on at least 70% of reckonable energy being intended for the eligible installation or site activity.
Eligibility is assessed at facility level under the scheme rules.
Eligibility determines scheme participation rather than a measured emissions quantity.
Energy-eligibility percentages must not be converted into greenhouse-gas values without factors and activity evidence.
No parcel emission is inferred.

packages.title: CCA Target Period 7 reporting deadline QA
facts: Target Period 7 runs from 1 January to 31 December 2026.
The stated deadline for Target Period 7 data submission is 1 May 2027.
Target Period 8 data are due 1 May 2029 and Target Period 9 data are due 1 May 2031.
Target reports compare performance with agreement targets.
A future target-period report must not be treated as current observed evidence.

packages.title: CCA performance target versus direct measurement QA
facts: CCA reporting is organised around target periods and performance against agreed targets.
Operators must remain eligible to hold an agreement.
Scheme performance information is tied to the CCA facility and reporting rules.
A target or compliance status is not equivalent to a parcel greenhouse-gas measurement.
No cadastral emissions value is created.

packages.title: CCA facility-level targets in new scheme QA
facts: The new CCA phase beginning in 2026 uses facility-level targets.
The biennial report describes this as replacing the previous bubbled approach covering multiple facilities.
The change is intended to strengthen incentives for energy efficiency or decarbonisation at sites.
A target architecture is not itself a measured emissions result.
No parcel value is inferred from target structure.

packages.title: CCA Climate Change Levy incentive boundary QA
facts: The CCA continuation keeps reduced Climate Change Levy rates in place into the scheme administration period, subject to policy rules.
Tax relief is a policy incentive linked to agreement compliance.
A levy discount is not an emissions quantity.
Financial treatment must not be used as a proxy for physical greenhouse-gas emissions.
No parcel emission value is inferred.

packages.title: REPD April 2026 database vintage QA
facts: The REPD quarterly extract page published the April 2026 database on 6 May 2026.
REPD tracks renewable-energy projects through planning and delivery stages.
The database is a project pipeline rather than a direct emissions inventory.
Dataset vintage must be preserved when comparing project status.
No parcel greenhouse-gas value is inferred from a planning record.

packages.title: REPD project status versus generation QA
facts: REPD includes projects at stages such as planning, consent, construction and operation.
A project recorded as planned or consented is not necessarily generating electricity.
Installed capacity and project status are distinct from actual generation.
Actual generation is distinct again from greenhouse-gas emissions.
No property-level emissions quantity is created.
